t: Louis became king at four, lived through the Fronde as a child, and from 1661 ruled without a chief minister, drawing the nobility to his court at Versailles and weakening their independent power.

France was the leading European power under him, but his wars against shifting alliances strained its finances, and the long war over the Spanish succession ended in 1713 and 1714 with France in major debt.

He banned Protestant worship by the Edict of Fontainebleau in 1685, after years of persecution and the quartering of dragoons in Protestant homes; historians still dispute how much the departure of some 200,000 Huguenots harmed France.
dyk: Louis was an eager dancer who performed 80 roles in 40 major ballets, among them Neptune and Apollo in Molière's Les Amants magnifiques in 1670.
ev: Louis is born at Saint-Germain-en-Laye after 23 years of his parents' marriage and is named Louis Dieudonné
He becomes king at the age of four on the death of Louis XIII, with his mother Anne of Austria as sole regent and Cardinal Mazarin as chief minister
After Mazarin's death Louis declares that he will rule without a chief minister
France invades the Dutch Republic, beginning the Franco-Dutch War, which ends with the Treaty of Nijmegen in 1678
The royal court moves officially to the Palace of Versailles
The Edict of Fontainebleau revokes the Edict of Nantes and ends the toleration of Protestants in France
The Peace of Utrecht ends the War of the Spanish Succession, leaving Philip V on the Spanish throne
Louis dies at Versailles and is succeeded by his five-year-old great-grandson, Louis XV

f.born: 5 September 1638 at the Château de Saint-Germain-en-Laye, as Louis Dieudonné; son of Louis XIII and Anne of Austria, of the House of Bourbon
f.died: 1 September 1715 at Versailles, of gangrene, four days before his 77th birthday; buried in the Basilica of Saint-Denis
f.role: King of France from 14 May 1643 until his death in 1715; under the regency of his mother Anne of Austria and the chief minister Cardinal Mazarin until 1661, then ruling without a chief minister
f.known: the longest reign of any monarch; the consolidation of absolute monarchy; the palace of Versailles and its court; the Franco-Dutch War, the Nine Years' War and the War of the Spanish Succession; the revocation of the Edict of Nantes; Colbert's financial and commercial reforms; patronage of Molière, Racine, Lully and Le Brun
